name: Adaptive Projected Guidance (core)
plain: Splits the guidance direction into a part along the positive prediction and a part across it, then weights them. It optionally averages the direction over steps and caps its norm. In core it rewrites cond before linear CFG, so later hooks see a modified cond, and the result carries one more unit of guidance than the Sana pack: with η=1 and no cap, core gives the effect of cfg s+1 even though its tooltip says default CFG behaviour. The Sana pack returns x̂_c+(s−1)·g' directly.
math:
g = x̂_c − x̂_u
momentum β≠0: v ← β·v + g, g ← v (v reset when sigma rises)
threshold T>0: g ← g·min(1, T/‖g‖₂) over last 3 dims
g∥ = (g·û)û with û = x̂_c/‖x̂_c‖ over last 3 dims; g⊥ = g − g∥
g' = g⊥ + η·g∥
x̂_c' = x̂_u + g' + (x̂_c−x̂_u)/s, then linear CFG.
Core result: x̂_cfg = x̂_u + s·g' + (x̂_c − x̂_u) = x̂_c + s·g'
Sana pack: x̂ = x̂_c + (s−1)·g', norms over [C,H,W] on 5-D latents in its default hw mode.

providers.author: smthemex
providers.note: Video norm dims chosen by mode hw (default), thw or t; momentum buffer and threshold as in core; rest of body not read

label: from code
surprise: The update has an extra (x̂_c−x̂_u) term beyond s·g′: the code adds (cond−uncond)/s to cond, so after CFG an unprojected guidance step at scale 1 remains. Effective form s·g′+Δ, not s·g′ alone.

audit.note: The math is right for core, but it is presented as one method with the Sana pack, which differs. Sana returns x̂_c + (s−1)·g' (Sana/diffusion/guiders/adaptive_projected_guidance.py:144), while core reduces to x̂_c + s·g' (ComfyUI/comfy_extras/nodes_apg.py:93 then samplers.py:598), one more unit of guidance. Sana on 5-D latents defaults to dims [C,H,W] (mode hw, lines 113, 119-120), not the last 3 dims. Plain's "aiming to allow high cfg with less over-saturation" is not stated in the code it cites. Core consequence worth stating: with η=1 and no threshold the result is x̂_u+(s+1)(x̂_c−x̂_u), although the eta tooltip says default CFG behaviour (nodes_apg.py:28).
